name: HALLIGAN, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the defendant's arrest was an unlawful "constructive entry" violating Payton and the State Constitution, and that the Appellate Division must re-evaluate the voluntariness of the third-party consent using the correct legal standard for the weapon possession charge.

name: SINGAS, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the Appellate Division correctly found the tenant's consent voluntary, that attenuation analysis is not applicable to third-party consent following a Payton violation, and that the majority's new "constructive entry" rule and State Constitution analysis are unpreserved and legally unsound.

name: WILSON, Chief Judge
description: Concurred, argued that political subdivisions generally lack the capacity to challenge state laws, and Newburgh failed to meet the narrow 'dilemma' exception for facial constitutional challenges.

name: TROUTMAN, J.
description: Concurred, argued that a defendant may forfeit the constitutional right to a trial by a jury of 12 persons through egregious, preplanned misconduct that interferes with jury deliberations and necessitates a juror's discharge when no alternate jurors are available.

name: GARCIA, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Even Year Election Law is a proper exercise of legislative authority and does not violate Article IX of the State Constitution.

name: CANNATARO, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Climate Act does not preempt local laws regulating greenhouse gas emissions, as the State Legislature did not express or imply an intent to occupy the entire field and explicitly encouraged complementary local action.

name: RIVERA, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Act is constitutional as New York's separation of powers is flexible, the Governor's appointment/removal powers are not exclusive, and the Act addresses the unique problem of executive self-regulation to restore public trust.

name: GARCIA, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the Act unconstitutionally encroaches on executive power by granting a legislative-appointed commission sweeping enforcement authority without sufficient gubernatorial oversight, violating separation of powers.

name: CANNATARO, Judge
description: Took no part in the decision.

name: WILSON, Chief Judge
description: Concurred, argued that Article II, Section 1 of the New York Constitution explicitly limits voting to citizens, and Local Law 11, which sought to enfranchise non-citizens, is unconstitutional.

name: RIVERA, J.
description: Dissented, argued that Article II, Section 1 of the State Constitution is an affirmative right for citizens and does not prohibit localities from expanding the franchise to non-citizens under home rule authority, and Local Law 11 should only be nullified for failing to hold a public referendum.

name: WILSON, Chief Judge
description: Concurred, argued that the New York Constitution does not explicitly require in-person voting and the removal of the Election District Provision in 1966, along with the legislature's plenary power over election methods, means the Early Mail Voter Act is constitutional despite a rejected ballot initiative.

name: RIVERA, J.
description: Concurred in result, argued that while the Constitution once required in-person voting, the 1966 amendment removed that requirement, and the current text does not prohibit mail-in voting, disagreeing with the majority's historical analysis and speculation about political motives.

name: GARCIA, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the Constitution has long been understood to limit absentee voting to specific categories, and the legislature's attempt to pass universal mail-in voting after voters rejected a constitutional amendment to do so disregards the People's will and violates constitutional limits.

name: HALLIGAN, J.
description: Concurred, argued that trial counsel was not ineffective for not requesting a cross-racial identification instruction because it was discretionary at the time and not an egregious single error.

name: WILSON, Chief Judge
description: Concurred, argued that counsel's representation was constitutionally sufficient as the mandatory instruction rule came after the trial, and counsel did request a general eyewitness unreliability charge.

name: TROUTMAN, J.
description: Dissented, argued that counsel was ineffective for failing to request a cross-racial identification charge, as its importance was widely understood, especially in a single-witness cross-racial identification case.

name: RIVERA, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the importance of cross-racial identification charges was well-recognized before Boone, making counsel's failure to request it ineffective assistance.

name: Wilson, Chief Judge
description: Concurred, argued that counsel's failure to request the appropriate jury instruction for the voluntary surrender defense, which was supported by trial testimony, constituted ineffective assistance of counsel, requiring a new trial.

name: CANNATARO, J.
description: Dissented, argued that counsel was not ineffective as the defendant was not entitled to a voluntary surrender instruction, and the majority's ruling ignores facts and poses a public safety risk.

name: RIVERA, J.
description: Concurred, argued that police interference with a bicyclist is a seizure requiring reasonable suspicion or probable cause, similar to automobile stops, and the officers in this case lacked such justification.

name: SINGAS, J.
description: Dissented, argued that police encounters with bicyclists should be evaluated on a case-by-case basis, not a per se seizure, and the officers had founded suspicion to conduct a common-law inquiry.

name: Judge Garcia
description: Dissented, argued that police encounters with bicyclists should be evaluated on a case-by-case basis, not a per se seizure, and the officers had founded suspicion to conduct a common-law inquiry.

name: Judge Cannataro

name: Chief Judge Wilson
description: Concurred, argued that the 2014 constitutional amendments limit court-drawn maps to only what is necessary to remedy a violation of law, and therefore the IRC has a continuing constitutional duty to produce new maps for future elections.

name: Judge Cannataro
description: Dissented, argued that the court-ordered maps from Harkenrider should remain in force until the next federal decennial census, and the majority's decision rewrites the Constitution and undermines the judiciary's role in safeguarding fair elections.

name: Judge Garcia
description: Dissented, argued that the court-ordered maps from Harkenrider should remain in force until the next federal decennial census, and the majority's decision rewrites the Constitution and undermines the judiciary's role in safeguarding fair elections.

name: Judge Singas
description: Dissented, argued that the court-ordered maps from Harkenrider should remain in force until the next federal decennial census, and the majority's decision rewrites the Constitution and undermines the judiciary's role in safeguarding fair elections.

name: GARCIA, J.
description: Concurred, argued that Administrative Code § 10-181 is a valid exercise of the City's municipal law-making authority, as it is neither preempted by state law nor unconstitutionally vague.

name: WILSON, CHIEF JUDGE
description: Concurred, argued that the legislature properly delegated authority to the Commission to promulgate Familial DNA Search Regulations.

name: LINDLEY, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the Commission overstepped its authority by engaging in legislative policy-making not authorized by the legislature when promulgating familial DNA search regulations.

name: Troutman
description: Dissented, argued that the Commission overstepped its authority by engaging in legislative policy-making not authorized by the legislature when promulgating familial DNA search regulations.

name: Lynch
description: Dissented, argued that the Commission overstepped its authority by engaging in legislative policy-making not authorized by the legislature when promulgating familial DNA search regulations.

name: Halligan

name: WILSON, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the People's unexplained four-year delay in filing an indictment, particularly 31 months of unexplained delay, violated the defendant's constitutional right to prompt prosecution, necessitating dismissal of the indictment.

name: SINGAS, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's decision improperly applied the balancing test for due process violations, undermining justice for sexual assault victims and reinforcing historical biases against them, especially given the seriousness of the crime and lack of actual prejudice to the defendant.

name: GARCIA, Judge
description: Dissented, argued for the reasons stated in Justice Christine M. Clark's Appellate Division dissenting opinion, which upheld the denial of the motion to dismiss on constitutional speedy trial grounds.

name: TROUTMAN, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the warrantless inspections authorized by the ELD rule fall within the administrative search exception to the warrant requirement and do not constitute unreasonable searches and seizures under the State Constitution.

name: CANNATARO, J.
description: Concurred, argued that Local Law No. 2 is consistent with state law and the New York Constitution, as RPTL article 11 permits cities to opt back in and does not require an agreement under RPTL 1150 for a county to enforce city taxes.

name: Judge Halligan
description: Other, took no part in the decision.

name: WILSON, CHIEF JUDGE
description: Concurred, argued that the police lacked reasonable suspicion to believe Mr. Johnson had committed a crime or was in possession of a weapon, and thus the evidence seized from the unjustified stop and frisk must be suppressed.

name: RIVERA, J.
description: Concurred, argued that while agreeing with the result, the De Bour framework itself is flawed and has proven counterproductive, failing to protect individuals from subconstitutional abuses and contributing to racial profiling and dangerous escalations in police encounters.

name: Cannataro, Acting Chief Judge
description: Concurred, argued that the enabling act was a valid assignment of power to the Committee, which operated within constitutional limits and standards, and did not exceed its authority.

name: WILSON, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Enabling Act, while weakening the Governor's ability to check excessive compensation, is constitutional under a narrow construction and heightened judicial scrutiny, ensuring the balance of power is maintained.

name: SINGAS, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the Enabling Act unconstitutionally delegated core legislative power to unelected individuals, violating the constitutionally mandated lawmaking process and separation of powers.

name: Garcia
description: Dissented, argued that the Enabling Act unconstitutionally delegated core legislative power to unelected individuals, violating the constitutionally mandated lawmaking process and separation of powers.

name: DiFIORE, Chief Judge
description: Concurred, argued that the legislature's redistricting maps were procedurally unconstitutional due to the IRC's failure to follow the mandated process and substantively unconstitutional due to partisan gerrymandering, requiring new maps.

name: TROUTMAN, J.
description: Dissented in part, argued that the majority's opinion on substantive gerrymandering was an inappropriate advisory opinion and that the legislature should be ordered to adopt one of the IRC-approved plans rather than having a court-appointed special master draw new maps.

name: WILSON, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the petitioners failed to prove beyond a reasonable doubt that the 2022 redistricting maps violated the Constitution through partisan gerrymandering, and agreed with Judge Troutman's proposed remedy.

name: RIVERA, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the legislature did not violate redistricting procedures or constitutional mandates, and petitioners failed to prove unconstitutional partisan gerrymandering.

name: WILSON, J.
description: Dissented, argued that Mr. Dawson unequivocally requested counsel, and the majority's decision vitiates the privilege against self-incrimination, right to counsel, and due process.

name: Judge Rivera
description: Concurred with Judge Wilson's dissenting opinion.

name: Chief Judge DiFIORE
description: Concurred, arguing that IFS contests are skill-based competitions, not games of chance or bets/wagers, and thus do not constitute prohibited gambling under the Constitution.

name: Judge WILSON
description: Dissented, arguing that IFS contests are clearly gambling under the common understanding of the term, and the majority's decision improperly redefines gambling, thereby usurping the constitutional process and legislative authority.

name: Judge Garcia
description: Took no part in the decision.

name: GARCIA, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Right of Way Law's ordinary negligence mens rea is constitutional and not preempted by state law, citing precedents for strict liability and ordinary negligence in criminal statutes, and affirming the City's authority to enact such laws.

name: WILSON, J.
description: Concurred, argued that while joining the majority's decision, the basis for the City's authority to criminalize traffic infractions is unclear, and the question of whether cities can criminalize violations designated as traffic infractions by the state remains unresolved.

name: Chief Judge DiFIORE
description: Concurred, argued that eavesdropping warrants are executed where law enforcement intentionally intercepts communications, regardless of the target's physical location, and that this interpretation ensures proper oversight and protects privacy.

name: Judge Wilson
description: Dissented, argued that New York law does not authorize a court to issue a warrant for diverting out-of-state cellular calls into New York for interception when neither the target nor the call participants are in New York, and that the majority's interpretation grants an unreasonable geographic reach to law enforcement.

name: Judge Rivera
description: Dissented, concurred with Judge Wilson's dissenting opinion.

name: RIVERA, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the construction of snowmobile trails requiring significant tree cutting and land alteration violates the "forever wild" provision of the New York State Constitution and requires a constitutional amendment.

name: STEIN, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the project does not constitute a "substantial change" to the Forest Preserve, is consistent with public use and protection, and that the majority misapplies precedent by requiring a constitutional amendment for a long-standing public use.

name: WILSON, J.
description: Concurred, argued that a search warrant for "entire premises" does not implicitly authorize the search of vehicles on the property without specific mention and probable cause for the vehicles themselves, upholding New York's stricter constitutional standards.

name: FEINMAN, J.
description: Dissented, argued that a valid warrant for "entire premises" should permit the search of vehicles parked on the premises if they could contain the items sought, viewing vehicles as containers and aligning with federal and other state court interpretations.

name: DiFIORE, C.J.
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's decision deviates from federal and other state court interpretations regarding premises warrants and vehicle searches.

name: GARCIA, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's decision deviates from federal and other state court interpretations regarding premises warrants and vehicle searches.
